atAGlance: Mì hoành thánh is wonton egg-noodle soup, usually with pork wontons, egg noodles, chives, and broth.
whatItIs: Mì hoành thánh is egg-noodle soup with wontons, a Vietnamese-Chinese shop classic. The bowl usually balances chewy yellow noodles, pork or shrimp wontons, greens, scallions, and a clear savory broth.
howToEnjoy: Taste a wonton and a spoonful of broth before adding chili oil. The best bowls have springy noodles, tender wontons, and broth that stays clean enough to sip.
howLocalsOrder: Order mì hoành thánh when you want the wontons to be the point of the bowl. Ask for less chili or chili on the side if the shop adds chili oil by default.
worthKnowing: This is part of Vietnam’s Chinese-influenced noodle-shop language, especially visible in southern cities and older market neighborhoods.
goodToKnow: Ask for không cay if you want Mì hoành thánh without added chili.
